title: Could Every PLANET Fit Between You and the Moon? 🌕
description:
Could every planet fit between you and the Moon? Yep. Line up Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune side by side and they come to about 388,000 km. The gap between Earth and the Moon, surface to surface, is about 398,000 km when the Moon is at its farthest. They fit, with about 10,000 km to spare. Jupiter and Saturn alone take up about two-thirds of it, and Saturn has to leave its rings behind: they are about 270,000 km across. The catch: the Moon's orbit is an oval, so every month it drifts in and out, by up to about 50,000 km. That's roughly one whole Neptune. On a close night the gap is only about 348,000 km, and Neptune is the one left outside. Did you think they'd fit?

The widths are NASA's equatorial diameters. The fact usually goes round as "they fit at the Moon's average distance" (384,400 km, measured centre to centre, with the planets' average widths, about 380,000 km); measured from your feet to the Moon's surface, they only fit when the Moon is far.

Bonus: the Moon drifts about 3.8 cm farther from Earth every year.
